name: Get client sign-off on ClickUp tasks by email with Claude, Gmail and Slack

parameters.content:
## Get client sign-off on ClickUp tasks by email with Claude, Gmail and Slack

### Who is it for

Agencies, studios and freelancers who run client work in ClickUp and lose days chasing approvals. Built for the account or project manager who sends work for review every week.

### How it works

1. Every 30 minutes, each task in your review status gets a review email to the client with the link to the work. By default it is saved as a Gmail draft so you can check the address and link before pressing Send. Tasks missing the client's email or the link are flagged once.
2. Claude reads each reply and labels it: approved, changes, question or unclear.
3. **Check Reply Against Email** is plain code. It confirms every quote is in the email and only lets a clear, unconditional approval through. A reply with a "but", a condition or a request comes to you instead.
4. Approvals move the task to your approved status. Change requests move it to your revisions status with the client's words as a checklist. The full reply is noted on the task and posted to Slack.
5. Bounces, out of office replies and replies from people not on the task never change anything. A waiting tag and a limit of 3 emails per task a day stop double emails.
6. Each morning you get one Slack summary, and quiet clients get a reminder saved as a Gmail draft, never sent.

### How to set up

- [ ] On each task, add the client's email and the review link as custom fields, or as description lines such as "Client Email: name@company.com" and "Review Link: https://...".
- [ ] Fill in **Config**: your workspace ID (the number after app.clickup.com/ in your browser), your three status names as ClickUp shows them, your name, business name and Slack channel ID (at the bottom of the channel details).
- [ ] Connect ClickUp, Gmail, Slack and Anthropic. Tags must be turned on in your ClickUp space.
- [ ] Publish, then move a task into your review status.

### Requirements

ClickUp, Gmail, Slack and an Anthropic API key. The 30 minute schedule uses about 1,500 runs a month.

### How to customize the workflow

Set sendMode to send to skip the drafts, and change the reminder days, approval phrases or lists in **Config**. Edit the email wording in **Work Out Review State**. To send a fresh review email for a task, remove its waiting tag.

## Run on a schedule

Every 30 minutes for replies and new reviews, plus a morning run for the summary.

## Check your settings

Fill in Config first. The check stops with a plain message if anything is missing.

## Find tasks in review

Every task in your review status, with the client email, name and review link.

## Close finished rounds

Tasks that left review lose the waiting tag, so the next round gets a fresh email.

## Read each task's notes

Reads every page of comments, so long task histories never cause a second email.

## Decide what each task needs

Send the review email, report a problem, or watch for a reply. Never more than 3 emails per task in 24 hours.

## Tag the task first

The waiting tag goes on before any email, so a failed run cannot email the client twice.

## Draft or send the review email

Draft by default, so you check the address and link before it goes. Gmail errors go to the problem notes.

## Note the email and alert

Writes the note the workflow reads later, then posts to Slack.

## Report problems

Missing details, refused emails and stuck tasks, noted once on the task and in Slack.

## Read the review threads

Picks out new messages and cuts quoted older emails. A deleted thread is reported once.

## Flag bounces and other senders

Bounces, empty replies and people not on the task never reach Claude and never change the task.

## Claude reads each reply

Claude labels the reply and copies the client's words. Swap the model if you prefer.

## Check Claude against the email

Plain code checks every quote. Only a clear approval with no condition or request moves the task.

## Move the task

Approved or changes status. Change requests become a checklist in the client's words.

## Note the reply and alert

The full reply goes on the task, and Slack gets a short alert with a link to the email.

## Morning summary

Unsent drafts, quiet clients and replies waiting on you, in one Slack message.

## Draft reminders

Quiet clients get a reminder saved as a Gmail draft. Nothing is sent.

options.systemMessage:
You read a client's email reply about work that was sent to them for review, and decide what they want. Fill in the JSON format.

decision, pick exactly one:
- approved: the client clearly signs off on the work as it is, with no conditions and no changes. Examples: "Approved", "Looks good, go ahead", "Happy with this, please publish it".
- changes_requested: the client asks for at least one change, however small, even if they also say they like the work.
- question: the client asks a question and does not approve or ask for changes yet.
- unclear: anything else.
These are not approvals, so choose unclear (or question) instead: praise without a clear sign-off ("Love it!", "Nice work"), a promise to decide later ("Looks good, I will check with my team"), an approval with a condition ("Approved once the typo is fixed"), approval of only part of the work, a request for more information ("Send me more details"), a thank you, or an out of office reply.
When in doubt, choose unclear. Never choose approved if any change is requested.

Fields:
- decision_quote: the client's sentence that shows the decision, copied word for word from the message. Empty for unclear.
- changes: one entry per change the client asked for. quote is the client's own words for that change, copied word for word from the message. change is a short instruction for the team, under 12 words. An empty list unless the decision is changes_requested.
- question: the client's question copied word for word, or an empty string.
- summary: one plain sentence about what the client said. Do not add anything they did not say.

The message may still contain a few lines quoted from older emails, including the email that asked for the review. Only use what the client wrote. A program checks every quote against the email and rejects anything that is not in it. Never paraphrase a quote, never fix the client's spelling and never join words from different sentences.

parameters.inputSchema: {"type": "object", "properties": {"decision": {"type": "string", "enum": ["approved", "changes_requested", "question", "unclear"]}, "decision_quote": {"type": "string", "description": "The client's sentence that shows the decision, word for word"}, "changes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"change": {"type": "string", "description": "Short instruction for the team"}, "quote": {"type": "string", "description": "The client's own words for this change, word for word"}}, "required": ["change", "quote"]}}, "question": {"type": "string", "description": "The client's question word for word, or an empty string"}, "summary": {"type": "string", "description": "One plain sentence"}}, "required": ["decision", "decision_quote", "changes", "question", "summary"]}
